exercise.name: 1 to 2 Jump Box
aliases: Single leg box jump, two foot landing

reference.title: 1 to 2 Jump Box (male)
reference.note: Used only to identify the movement. This rig, artwork and animation are original.

equipment: Plyo box (45 cm shown; foam or soft-top preferred)
exercise.laterality: Unilateral takeoff, bilateral landing (alternate the takeoff leg, equal reps per leg)

muscleNotes.quads_r: Takeoff leg: extends the knee in the drive, then absorbs the landing with the other leg.
muscleNotes.glute_max_r: Takeoff leg: drives hip extension. Single-leg takeoffs lean more on the hip than two-leg takeoffs.
muscleNotes.calves_r: Takeoff leg: the last push through the ball of the foot (ankle plantarflexion).
muscleNotes.quads_l: Shares the two-foot landing: controls knee bend into the quarter-to-half squat.
muscleNotes.glute_max_l: Shares the landing: controls the hips sitting back.
muscleNotes.hamstrings_r: Helps extend the hip at takeoff.
muscleNotes.adductors_r: Adductor magnus helps extend the hip at takeoff.
muscleNotes.hip_flexors_l: Swing leg: drives the free knee up so both feet meet in flight.
muscleNotes.hip_flexors_r: Takeoff leg: pulls the knee up after toe-off to join the swing leg.
muscleNotes.calves_l: Controls the ankle as the foot lands on the box.
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_r: Arm swing forward and up adds to the takeoff.
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_l: Arm swing forward and up adds to the takeoff.
muscleNotes.glute_med_r: Keeps the takeoff knee over the foot and the pelvis level on one leg.
muscleNotes.glute_med_l: Keeps the knees tracking over the toes on the landing.
muscleNotes.core: Braces the trunk through takeoff, flight and landing.
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_r: Holds the inclined trunk at takeoff and on the landing.
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_l: Holds the inclined trunk at takeoff and on the landing.

breathing.pattern: Inhale as you step into the stagger and load; exhale sharply as you drive off the takeoff leg; hold a brace through flight and the landing; breathe normally as you stand and step down.
breathing.cadence: About 1.2 s set and load, 0.4 s drive, 0.4 s flight, 0.7 s land and stick, then a calm step down and reset

prescription.reps: 3–5 per takeoff leg; never to failure
prescription.rest: Full rest between sets (sources give no seconds; 60–90 s is an unsourced app default)
prescription.frequency: 2–3 sessions per week, 48–72 h between plyometric sessions
prescription.boxHeight: Start at 30–46 cm; raise it only while the landing stays quiet, balanced and in a half squat
prescription.tempo: Explosive takeoff, soft stick, step down under control

cues.text: Stand tall a short step behind the box (toes about 30–35 cm away), arms at your sides, light brace.
Step the other foot back into a staggered stance with the takeoff foot in front. Breathe in.
Hinge slightly forward, bend into the front leg and draw both arms back.
Drive off the front leg through hip, knee and ankle as both arms swing forward and up. Breathe out on the drive.
Pull the free knee up and bring the takeoff leg to meet it, so both feet arrive together.
Land softly on both feet, whole feet on the box top. Hips back into a quarter-to-half squat, knees over toes, arms forward. Stick it for a beat.
Stand up tall on the box.
Step down backward one foot at a time; do not jump down.
Step back to the start, reset, then repeat or switch takeoff leg.

mistakes.mistake: Box too high: tucking the knees hard to clear the edge and landing in a deep squat
mistakes.fix: Use a lower box. Land in about the same half squat you took off from.
Land quietly with soft knees and hips back so the big muscles absorb the load.

mistakes.mistake: Knees caving inward on takeoff or landing
mistakes.fix: Keep the knees over the middle toes. Lower the box or go back to two-foot takeoffs until it is clean.

mistakes.mistake: Toes catching the box edge, or landing half on the box
mistakes.fix: Start close enough, jump up and slightly forward, and land with whole feet on the box top.

mistakes.mistake: One foot lands first, or the weight shifts to the takeoff side
mistakes.fix: Bring the takeoff leg up to meet the swing leg in flight and land both feet at once.
Step down. Jumping down turns every rep into a drop landing with extra Achilles and knee load.

mistakes.mistake: Only training the dominant takeoff leg
mistakes.fix: Alternate legs and match reps per side.

kinematics.measure: Takeoff knee at the bottom of the load (front leg)
kinematics.norm: No measured norm for this exercise; a shallow single-leg countermovement

kinematics.peak: Inclined forward ≈19° at the bottom of the load, ≈10° at toe-off, with the arm swing
kinematics.norm: Slightly forward trunk on a single-leg push-off
Settled quarter-to-half squat, animation estimate 45–75°. Indirect: 16–29° at contact and 81–96° peak in 30–31 cm drop landings (upper bounds; a box-top landing falls less)
Hips back, chest slightly forward. Indirect: 77–86° at peak knee flexion in drop landings
Indirect: about 3.0 × body weight for single-leg jumps vs 1.6–2.0 × for two-leg jumps

kinematics.setup: 45 cm (about knee height on this 172 cm rig)
kinematics.norm: Beginners 30–46 cm (12–18 in), raised as landing mechanics improve

cautions: Slipping off the box edge causes most box jump lower-leg wounds: use a foam or soft-top box on a non-slip floor and land with whole feet on the top.
The takeoff leg takes roughly 3 × body weight; stop the set if landings get loud, stiff or uneven. Do not train it fatigued.
modify: Acute or subacute ankle or knee sprain, acute inflammation, recent surgery, joint instability, history of stress injuries or poor base strength: use a low box, a two-foot takeoff or a step-up instead.
Knee pain, patellar or Achilles tendinopathy, or prior ACL injury: get clinician clearance; keep the box low and use step-downs only.
Knees caving in or stiff landings: go back to landing drills first; technique feedback raises landing knee flexion within a few sessions.
regressions: Two-foot takeoff box jump onto a low box.
progressions: Raise the box gradually while the landing stays quiet and in a half squat.
Single-leg landing (same-leg or opposite-leg) on a low box.
